To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we determined the solution structure of the ETO TAF homology domain (TAFH) and that this structure is similar to the TAFH domain of Sin3, a transcriptional co-repressor that is known to interact with E-proteins.
we solved the structure of the TAFH domain of the ETO protein and that the TAFH of ETO is similar to the paired amphipath helix domain of the Sin3 transcriptional corepressor.

we solved the 3D structure of the ETO TAFh domain and that the structure of the Eto TAFh domain has a fold similarity to paired-amphipathic helices and that the TAFh domain of the ETO corepressor is essential for its interaction with the E protein transcription factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms by which ETO and AML1- ETO inhibit transcriptional activation by the E proteins.
the molecular mechanisms of transcriptional regulation in normal and malignant hematopoietic cells and the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of hematological malignancies.
the molecular mechanism of the t(8; 21) chromosomal aberration in AML.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AML1- ETO fusion protein targets E proteins via an eTAFH domain that shares a fold similarity to the paired amphipath helix domains of the corepressor Sin3 and that eTAF H is essential for AML1-ET O-mediated repression of E protein transac tivation.
the AML1-ET0 protein is an aberrant fusion protein, and it can cause the development of leukemia.
AML1- ETO is a novel transcriptional repressor that inhibits E protein activity via a cofactor exchange process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AML1- ETO inhibits E protein transactivation through a novel mechanism involving eTAFH-dependent displacement of coactivators.
the AML1- ETO fusion protein inhibits E protein transactivation via a TBP- associated factor homology domain that binds to and replaces WT coactivators.

we have identified a conserved domain in ETO that mediates the corepression of E proteins and that the eTAFH domain is likely to be a novel target for the development of therapeutic strategies for the t(8; 21) subtype of AML.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ETO is a transcriptional corepressor that can inhibit E protein transactivator activity.
the AML1-eto fusion protein targets E proteins via an unexpected TAFH domain that may serve as a novel target for therapeutic intervention.
AML1-ETOs TAFH domain, like Sin3s PHD, is a protein-protein interaction domain, not a DNA binding domain.
